headline: New evening confusion since about mid-October, including a stove left on, together with caregiver exhaustion and a respite request, needs team review. The chart does not show the planned work-up results.

items.statement: On 2026-11-02 his grandson Robert reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. Jerónimo was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, a medication review and a PCP visit that week. The notes and record:encounters show no results or visit after that date.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 2026-11-02 nursing note; empty encounters record supports no visit/results recorded afterward.

items.statement: On 2026-11-22 Robert, the primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. The social worker discussed respite options and a caregiver support group.
items.verifier_note: Matches the 2026-11-22 social work note in every detail.

items.statement: The fall entry dated 2026-09-25 was corrected on 2026-09-26 as documented on the wrong participant, and the social worker confirmed this on 2026-09-29. The PT evaluation of 2026-09-29 (gait slow and unsteady, TUG 19 seconds, walker and home safety recommendations) cites that fall, so the team should verify that it applies to him.
items.verifier_note: Correction on 09-26, SW confirmation on 09-29, and PT eval details (gait, TUG 19s, walker, home safety) all match; PT eval cites the Sep 25 fall, and flagging for verification is appropriate.

items.statement: Care gap: no influenza vaccine is recorded this season (season start 2026-08-01). The most recent dose was 2026-06-30.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on 2026-11-02 completed, and what did they show?
What interim safety measures are needed for the evenings, given the stove incident and Robert's concern about managing alone?
Can respite and caregiver support be arranged promptly for Robert?
Does the PT evaluation of 2026-09-29 and its walker and home-safety recommendations still apply, given the fall entry was a charting error?
Should the influenza vaccine be offered now?

checks: Confirm review window 2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30 and identify what changed since the last IDT review (enrollment 2024-04-21 baseline).
Cardiac events: review for chest pain, nitroglycerin use frequency, ED visits or admissions, and any ECG or cardiology follow-up, given new ischemic heart disease onset 2026-06-30.

Antiplatelet and cardiac medication check: confirm clopidogrel, metoprolol succinate, simvastatin, and SL nitroglycerin were started 2026-07-07 as intended; check adherence, dizziness, heart rate and blood pressure trend, bleeding signs, and any missed refills.
Bleeding risk review: look for GI bleeding, bruising, hematuria, dental bleeding (impacted molars on problem list), and any dental extractions or procedures that may need antiplatelet coordination.

Osteoporosis treatment: confirm alendronic acid adherence since 2026-06-30 (upright posture, fasting administration), check for dysphagia, heartburn, or new back or hip pain, and confirm calcium and vitamin D status and fracture history.
Falls and fracture check: any falls, near-falls, or fractures in window, especially with new beta-blocker, antiplatelet, and nitrate use, and with scoliosis and osteoporosis.

Substance use review: dependent drug abuse on record since 2018; review opioid or other controlled substance prescriptions, pharmacy fill patterns, early refill requests, urine drug screen results, any relapse, and naloxone availability, given chronic pain and migraine.

Pain and migraine review: chronic pain and chronic intractable migraine; track headache days, analgesic use, pain scores, and whether any medication changes or stops occurred; check for interactions with clopidogrel (e.g., NSAID use) and nitrates.
Weight and BMI trend: obesity on record since 1990; review weights over window, dietary and activity changes, and whether cardiac diet counseling or referral is due.
Function and ADLs: review IADL and ADL changes, mobility, ability to manage medications, and any new home supports or equipment needs, given scoliosis and chronic pain.
Cognition and mood: screen for changes in memory, mood, or sleep, and for depression or anxiety after new cardiac diagnosis; check attendance at PACE day programs, transport, and missed appointments.
Caregiver and social situation: confirm current caregiver availability, living situation, San Diego transport access, and any caregiver strain noted since the last review.

Care-plan items due: confirm due dates for cardiology follow-up, lipid and renal labs after statin and antiplatelet start, bone density follow-up, dental care, and advance directive and code status review after the new cardiac diagnosis.
Allergies: record shows none; verify with the participant and pharmacy, since this is a new medication regimen.
